**The Battle Over the Ballroom**

**Anthropic Researcher Quits Over AI Safety Fears; Congressional Reaction Spreads**
Jacob Coxon, a researcher at leading artificial intelligence company Anthropic, announced on Wednesday that he was leaving the company due to concerns about the catastrophic risks posed by further AI development. “We’re on track for a lot of the most aggressive of these scenarios where by the end of next year things could be out of control already,” Coxon told the *Wall Street Journal*, referring to his belief that leading AI companies were nearing the ability to create continuously self-improving and potentially uncontrollable models. Evan Hubinger, one of Anthropic's top AI safety executives, who remains at the company, responded by tweeting that AI safety researchers “really do earnestly believe AI could kill all humans! I personally think it is greater than 10% within the next decade.”

Senator Ted Cruz, a Republican from Texas, stated in a TV interview that he was working with other senators on AI safety legislation, saying, “This is scary stuff, but we’re also not going to be able to stick our head in the sand and pretend technology isn’t happening. So we’ve got to put some guardrails on it.” Meanwhile, Senator Bernie Sanders, a Democrat from Vermont, informed colleagues that he would hold a private briefing for senators with AI safety researchers next week, emphasizing that “Congress needs SERIOUS discussions about this issue.”

**GOP Convention Begins in Dallas**
The Republican Party kicked off an unusual midterm convention in Dallas on Wednesday, aimed at galvanizing GOP voters with less than two months remaining until Election Day. President Donald Trump delivered the keynote speech for the two-day event, stating that the Democratic Party was too left-wing to be trusted with political power. “If we hand America’s future to the radical-left Democrats, our nation will spend the next decade just getting back on its feet. It’ll be a tragedy,” he told the crowd at American Airlines Center. Trump framed the election as a referendum on himself, urging the crowd, “I am asking you to pretend I’m on the ballot. I’m on the ballot. I’m on the ballot. Just one more time.”

In a surprise video appearance, Democratic Senator John Fetterman of Pennsylvania addressed the crowd and praised his fellow Pennsylvania senator, Republican Dave McCormick. “I’m always going to stand with America. I’m always going to reject the extremes and socialism and that anti-American way of life,” Fetterman stated. He has recently clashed with his party over his strong pro-Israel stance, a divide that has grown wider in recent months.

The last major party midterm convention occurred in 1982, when the Democrats met in Philadelphia. Party leaders subsequently decided to abandon the practice in 1986, and neither party has held one since.

**Iran and the U.S. Trade Escalating Strikes on Shipping**
Iran and the U.S. engaged in dueling strikes on merchant shipping on Tuesday and Wednesday, with each side attacking commercial vessels. After U.S. Central Command reported the destruction of five Iranian oil tankers, the Iranian government claimed to have fired on two U.S. naval vessels and eight oil tankers near the Strait of Hormuz in retaliation. An Iranian military spokesman announced that Iran would attack 20 targets for every two or three U.S. strikes moving forward.

The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency reported a vessel listing in the ocean off the coast of the United Arab Emirates and multiple merchant vessels in the Southern Arabian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman coming under “disabling fire.” The tanker chartering company Peninsula reported that one of its vessels anchored off Dubai was attacked, resulting in one sailor's death and another missing. Jordan also reported intercepting 18 Iranian missiles, with two landing in unpopulated areas.

In response to these tensions, Brent crude oil prices rose to $100 a barrel for the first time since July. President Trump stated he does not expect oil prices to decline until after the midterm elections in November, although he anticipates the Iranian regime will back down afterward.
